fields.heading: Engineers first
fields.body:
Mehr Cool Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Ltd was incorporated in May 2024 and is based in Canary Wharf. The company was founded by working refrigeration engineers who had spent years watching good equipment fail for avoidable reasons: dirty condensers, skipped leak checks, undersized plant and paperwork nobody kept.

We run the business the way we would want a contractor to run it for us. The engineer who quotes the job is the engineer who installs it. Every visit ends with a written report. Every gram of refrigerant is recorded.

24/7 :: Emergency line answered by an engineer

100% :: Engineers F-Gas certified
10+ :: Manufacturers installed and maintained

fields.heading: Why F-Gas matters to you
fields.items:
It is the law :: Anyone handling fluorinated refrigerants in the UK must hold an F-Gas certificate. Using an uncertified contractor exposes the equipment owner to enforcement action, not just the contractor.
Leak checks are mandatory :: Systems containing 5 tonnes CO₂-equivalent or more must be leak-tested at fixed intervals and the results recorded. We calculate the threshold for every asset and schedule accordingly.
Records protect you :: Insurers, landlords and auditors ask for refrigerant logs. Ours are issued after every visit and kept for five years, as the regulation requires.

fields.heading: Company details
fields.body:
**Legal name:** MEHR COOL REFRIGERATION & AIR CONDITIONING LTD

**Company number:** 15733975 (registered in England and Wales)

**Registered office:** Dept 2710, 126 East Ferry Road, Canary Wharf, London, E14 9FP

**Principal activity:** SIC 43220 — Plumbing, heat and air-conditioning installation

## Our obligations
Mehr Cool Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Ltd handles fluorinated greenhouse gases (F-Gases) in the course of installing, maintaining and decommissioning refrigeration and air conditioning equipment. We operate under the F-Gas Regulation (EC 517/2014, as retained in UK law) and the associated UK company certification requirements.

## Certification
- Every engineer who handles refrigerant holds a valid F-Gas category certificate.
- The company holds, or is in the process of obtaining, company certification through a recognised UK scheme. Certificate numbers are shown on our accreditation badges once issued and are available on request.

## What we do on every job
- Recover refrigerant rather than vent it, using certified recovery equipment.
- Weigh and record all refrigerant added or removed, by type and quantity.
- Issue a written record to the equipment operator after every intervention.
- Leak-test systems at the intervals the regulation requires, based on CO₂-equivalent charge.
- Label equipment with refrigerant type, charge and GWP.

## Refrigerant choice
For new installations we specify low-GWP refrigerants — R32 for air conditioning, R290 (propane) or R448A/R449A for commercial refrigeration — so that equipment we install today remains serviceable through the HFC phase-down.

## Questions
If you are an equipment operator and unsure of your own obligations, ask us. We will explain what applies to your systems in plain English.

## 1. These terms
These terms of business apply to all quotations, installations, maintenance contracts and repair work carried out by MEHR COOL REFRIGERATION & AIR CONDITIONING LTD (company number 15733975), referred to as "we" or "us".

## 2. Quotations
Written quotations are valid for 30 days unless stated otherwise. Prices exclude VAT unless shown as inclusive. Work outside the quoted scope is agreed in writing before it starts.

## 3. Emergency callouts
Emergency attendance is charged at the rate stated when the call is booked, including any out-of-hours uplift. Parts and refrigerant are charged in addition unless a fixed price is agreed.

## 4. Payment
Invoices are payable within 30 days. We may charge statutory interest on late payment. Title to equipment passes on full payment.

## 5. Warranty
Our workmanship is guaranteed for 12 months. Manufacturer warranties apply to equipment and may require a maintenance contract to remain valid.

## 6. Access and site conditions
You agree to provide safe access, power and water where needed. Delays caused by access restrictions may be charged.

## 7. Liability
Nothing in these terms limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence. Our liability for other losses is limited to the value of the work concerned.

## 8. Governing law
These terms are governed by the law of England and Wales.

## Who we are
MEHR COOL REFRIGERATION & AIR CONDITIONING LTD, Dept 2710, 126 East Ferry Road, Canary Wharf, London, E14 9FP, is the data controller for personal data collected through this website.

## What we collect
- Contact details you submit through our forms (name, phone, email, company, message).
- Technical information about your visit (pages viewed, device type) via analytics cookies, where you consent.

## Why we collect it
To respond to your enquiry, arrange engineer visits, prepare quotations and, if you become a customer, deliver our services and keep the legal records the F-Gas regulation requires.

## Legal basis
Responding to enquiries: our legitimate interest and steps towards a contract. Service records: legal obligation. Analytics: consent.

## How long we keep it
Enquiry data is kept for 24 months. Customer and refrigerant records are kept for at least five years as required by law.

## Your rights
You may ask for a copy of your data, correction, deletion or restriction of processing. Contact us using the details on the Contact page. You may also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office.

## Essential cookies
We set a session cookie and a security (CSRF) cookie so our forms work. These do not track you and cannot be switched off.

## Analytics cookies
If Google Analytics or Google Tag Manager is enabled on this site, Google may set cookies to measure how the site is used. IP addresses are anonymised. You can block these cookies in your browser without affecting the site.

## Third-party content
Embedded maps and videos may set their own cookies when loaded. We use privacy-enhanced embeds where available.

## Refrigeration & air conditioning engineers
We are a small, growing company based in Canary Wharf and we hire engineers who take pride in a tidy install and an honest diagnosis.

**You will need:**
- F-Gas Category 1 certification
- Experience on commercial refrigeration (cold rooms, display, cellar cooling) or VRF/split air conditioning — ideally both
- A full UK driving licence
- The ability to explain a fault to a chef at 11pm without jargon

**We offer:**
- Competitive salary with paid on-call and overtime
- Company van, tools and manufacturer training
- A say in how the company is run

Send a short note about your experience to the email address on our Contact page. No agencies.

fields.name: VRF/VRV Installation
fields.short_summary: Design and installation of multi-zone VRF/VRV climate control for offices, hotels and mixed-use buildings.
fields.intro:
Variable Refrigerant Flow (VRF — Daikin's trademark is VRV) connects one outdoor condensing unit to many indoor units, each modulating independently. That means individual zone control, simultaneous heating and cooling with heat-recovery systems, and lower running costs than multiple split systems.

We survey heat loads room by room, size pipework and refrigerant charge to manufacturer software, and commission every indoor unit with recorded superheat, subcooling and airflow figures. You receive as-installed drawings, the F-Gas record and the commissioning pack.
fields.price_from_note: Design and quote free for commercial sites

fields.name: Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM)
fields.short_summary: Scheduled servicing that keeps air conditioning compliant, efficient and out of the breakdown log.
fields.intro:
A PPM contract is a schedule of visits — usually two or four a year — where we clean coils and filters, check refrigerant charge and leak-test the circuit, verify controls and drains, and record everything in a service report you can hand to an auditor.

Under the F-Gas regulation, systems containing the equivalent of 5 tonnes of CO₂ or more must be leak-checked at fixed intervals. We track the CO₂-equivalent charge of every asset on your schedule and time inspections accordingly, so compliance is automatic rather than a scramble.
fields.price_from_note: From £45 per indoor unit per visit

fields.name: Air Conditioning Repairs
fields.short_summary: Fault-finding and repair on all major brands: refrigerant leaks, compressors, PCBs, fans and controls.
fields.intro:
Most air conditioning faults present as one of a handful of symptoms — not cooling, tripping, leaking water, error codes — and each has a short list of causes. Our engineers arrive with gauges, electronic leak detectors and the common parts for Daikin, Mitsubishi Electric, Toshiba and Fujitsu systems, so first-visit fix rates stay high.

If a repair is uneconomic we tell you, with a written comparison against replacement.

fields.name: Split System Installation
fields.short_summary: Wall, cassette and ducted split systems for single rooms, small offices, shops and server rooms.
fields.intro:
A split system pairs one outdoor unit with one (single split) or several (multi-split) indoor units. It is the right answer for a shop, a meeting room, a small office or a comms room that needs reliable cooling without the scale of VRF.

Server and comms rooms get particular attention: we specify units rated for continuous low-ambient operation and, where uptime matters, install duty/standby pairs with automatic changeover.
fields.typical_response_time: Installed within 10 working days of order
fields.price_from_note: Single wall-mounted system from £1,650 + VAT installed

fields.name: Walk-In Cold Rooms
fields.short_summary: Modular walk-in cold rooms designed, built and commissioned for kitchens, food retail and pharmacies.
fields.intro:
A walk-in cold room is a building inside your building: insulated panels, a door that seals, an evaporator matched to the load and a condensing unit sited where it can reject heat. Get the sizing wrong and the room struggles on the first hot Saturday in July.

We calculate the load from product throughput, door openings, ambient temperature and lighting, then specify panels (typically 80–100 mm for chilled rooms) and plant with 20–25% headroom. Commissioning includes pull-down to temperature, defrost cycle proving and a temperature logger left running for 24 hours.

fields.name: Display Refrigeration
fields.short_summary: Multideck, serve-over and island display cabinets for food retail, delis and convenience stores.
fields.intro:
Display refrigeration works hardest in the worst conditions: open-fronted, under shop lighting, opposite a door that never shuts. We supply, install and maintain multidecks, serve-overs, patisserie cabinets and island freezers — integral units for smaller stores and remote-plant cabinets on a pack system for supermarkets.

Maintenance focuses on the things that fail: fan motors, door gaskets, defrost heaters and condenser cleanliness. A dirty condenser can add 20% to running costs before it causes a breakdown.
fields.price_from_note: Maintenance from £38 per cabinet per visit

fields.name: Cellar Cooling
fields.short_summary: Beer cellar cooling installation and repair for pubs, bars and restaurants — keeping kegs at 11–13 °C.
fields.intro:
Cask and keg beer wants a cellar between 11 °C and 13 °C. Too warm and the beer fobs and spoils; too cold and cask ale goes hazy. Cellar cooling units are simple, but they run continuously in a damp room and fail quietly — usually on the hottest weekend of the year.

We install ceiling-mounted and split cellar coolers sized to cellar volume and keg throughput, and offer a pre-summer service that cleans coils, checks charge and tests the thermostat before the heat arrives.

fields.name: Freezer Rooms
fields.short_summary: Walk-in freezer rooms to -22 °C with insulated floors, heated door frames and alarmed controls.
fields.intro:
Freezer rooms are cold rooms with less margin for error. Panels are thicker (100–150 mm), the floor must be insulated, door frames are heated to stop ice bridging, and the evaporator needs a reliable defrost so it does not become a block of ice.

We build freezer rooms for kitchens, food manufacturers and pharmaceutical storage, with temperature alarms that call your phone if the room drifts — because product loss in a freezer is measured in thousands of pounds.

fields.name: 24/7 Emergency Callout
fields.short_summary: Rapid-response diagnosis and repair for refrigeration and air conditioning breakdowns, day and night.
fields.intro:
Call the emergency line and you speak to an engineer, not an answering service. We ask three questions — what has failed, where, and what the display says — then dispatch the nearest duty engineer with the likely parts.

On arrival we stabilise first (temporary plant, refrigerant top-up, bypass), then diagnose and repair or quote. Every emergency visit ends with a written report, including the refrigerant record.

fields.question: How long does a VRF installation take?
fields.answer: A single-floor office of around 400 m² is typically installed and commissioned in one to two weeks. Larger or occupied buildings are phased floor by floor so tenants keep working.

fields.question: Can VRF heat as well as cool?
fields.answer: Yes. Heat pump VRF switches the whole system between heating and cooling; heat recovery VRF lets some rooms heat while others cool at the same time, moving energy between them.

fields.question: Do I need planning permission for the outdoor units?
fields.answer: Often not, but listed buildings, conservation areas and some leases have restrictions on external plant. We check this during the survey and prepare acoustic data where required.

fields.question: Is PPM a legal requirement?
fields.answer: F-Gas leak checking is a legal requirement for systems above 5 tonnes CO₂-equivalent. Beyond that, PPM is how you meet insurer, landlord and TM44 obligations and keep the manufacturer's warranty valid.

fields.question: What happens if you find a fault during a visit?
fields.answer: Minor items are fixed on the spot where parts allow. Anything larger is quoted the same day with a fixed price, and contract clients receive discounted labour.

fields.question: My unit shows an error code — what should I do?
fields.answer: Note the code and, if safe, switch the unit off at the isolator. Send us a photo of the display by WhatsApp and we can often tell you the likely fault and bring the right part.

fields.question: How noisy is the outdoor unit?
fields.answer: Modern inverter units run at 45–55 dB(A) at one metre — comparable to a quiet conversation. We position and mount them to keep noise away from neighbours and bedrooms.

fields.question: How long does it take to build a cold room?
fields.answer: A standard 3 m × 3 m chilled room is typically built and commissioned in two days. Freezer rooms and rooms with insulated floors take three to four.

fields.question: Can you fit a cold room in a basement kitchen?
fields.answer: Yes — panels are modular and carried in by hand. The main constraint is heat rejection: we route the condensing unit to an external wall or a ventilated plant area.

fields.question: Which refrigerant will you use?
fields.answer: For new plant we default to R290 (propane) or a low-GWP HFO blend. Both meet current and forthcoming F-Gas phase-down rules, so you are not buying obsolescence.

fields.question: Can you retrofit doors to open multidecks?
fields.answer: Yes. Glass-door retrofits typically cut cabinet energy use by 30–40% and hold temperature more consistently. We measure the cabinet and source doors to fit.

fields.question: The cellar is warm but the unit is running — what's wrong?
fields.answer: Usually a dirty condenser, a low refrigerant charge or a failed fan. Prop the cellar door shut, avoid loading warm stock, and call us — this is the most common summer emergency we attend.

fields.question: How long will a freezer hold temperature in a power cut?
fields.answer: A well-built, full freezer room with the door shut will typically stay below -12 °C for six to eight hours. Keep the door closed and call us; we can bring temporary plant if the outage is prolonged.

fields.question: What counts as an emergency?
fields.answer: Any failure that puts stock, product or people at risk: a cold or freezer room warming, display cabinets off, a server room overheating, or air conditioning failure in a care setting. If you are unsure, call — we will tell you honestly whether it can wait until morning.

fields.question: Do you charge more at night and weekends?
fields.answer: Out-of-hours attendance carries an uplift, which we state on the phone before dispatching. Contract clients receive priority response and discounted rates.

fields.title: Walk-in freezer replacement for a Soho restaurant group
fields.summary: A failing 1990s freezer room feeding three restaurants was replaced in a 48-hour window without a single lost service.
fields.challenge: The group's central production kitchen ran one ageing freezer room serving three Soho restaurants. The R404A plant was leaking, the floor had lifted, and each breakdown meant hiring a refrigerated trailer at short notice. A full replacement had been put off for two years because the kitchen could not close.
fields.solution: We surveyed on a Monday, agreed a Sunday-to-Tuesday programme, and hired a temporary cold store for the changeover. The old room was stripped and a new 100 mm PIR freezer room with insulated floor, heated door frame and R449A remote condensing unit was built and commissioned inside the window. A high-temperature alarm now calls the head chef and our duty engineer.
fields.result: Zero services lost. Energy monitoring over the first quarter showed a 31% reduction in refrigeration electricity against the old plant, and emergency callouts for the freezer dropped from six in the previous year to none. The group moved all three sites onto a PPM contract.
fields.hero_image_alt: Walk-in freezer replacement for a Soho restaurant group — placeholder image

fields.title: Bringing 42 VRF indoor units back into F-Gas compliance
fields.anonymised_label: A serviced-office operator in Canary Wharf
fields.summary: An office operator inherited a VRF estate with no leak-check history. We audited every asset, repaired two leaks and put the building on a compliant PPM schedule.
fields.challenge: A new building manager discovered that the previous contractor had left no F-Gas records for four floors of Daikin VRV. With a landlord audit approaching, the operator needed the estate surveyed, any leaks fixed and a defensible maintenance schedule — quickly, and without disturbing tenants.
fields.solution: We tagged and logged all 42 indoor units and three outdoor systems, calculated CO₂-equivalent charge per circuit, and carried out electronic leak detection over two out-of-hours visits. Two leaking flare joints were repaired and recharged, coils and filters cleaned throughout, and a quarterly PPM schedule set with leak-check intervals matched to each circuit's charge.
fields.result: The landlord audit passed with a complete asset register and leak-check log. Tenant comfort complaints fell from an average of nine a month to two over the following quarter, and the operator has since added a second building to the contract.
fields.hero_image_alt: Bringing 42 VRF indoor units back into F-Gas compliance — placeholder image

fields.title: Glass-door retrofit cuts a convenience store's cabinet energy by 36%
fields.summary: Doors, EC fans and a condenser clean turned a struggling multideck line into the store's quietest, cheapest-to-run asset.
fields.challenge: Fourteen open multideck cabinets on a remote pack were struggling to hold temperature on warm afternoons, and the store's electricity bill had risen sharply. The owner assumed the pack needed replacing.
fields.solution: Inspection showed the pack was healthy but the condenser was heavily fouled and the cabinets were fighting a warm shop. We cleaned and pressure-washed the condenser, replaced the shaded-pole evaporator fans with EC motors, and fitted retrofit glass doors to all fourteen cabinets over two nights.
fields.result: Sub-metered cabinet energy fell by 36% against the same month the previous year, product temperatures stabilised within the 1–4 °C band, and the pack's run hours dropped enough to defer replacement by an estimated five years. Payback on the retrofit is projected at 22 months.

fields.title: Duty/standby cooling for a City law firm's comms room
fields.client_name: A City of London law firm
fields.anonymised_label: A City of London law firm
fields.summary: A single ageing wall unit was the only thing keeping a firm's servers cool. We replaced it with a monitored duty/standby pair.
fields.challenge: The firm's comms room relied on one 7 kW wall-mounted split that had already failed twice, each time taking the practice management system offline. There was no alerting; the first sign of trouble was staff noticing the room was hot.
fields.solution: We installed two 8 kW low-ambient ducted units with an automatic changeover controller that alternates duty weekly and brings the standby online on fault or high temperature. A temperature and fault relay now alerts both the IT manager and our duty engineer.
fields.result: No cooling-related downtime since commissioning. The monitoring caught a condensate pump fault within weeks — the standby took over automatically and the repair was made during working hours without anyone in the office noticing.

fields.name: City of London
fields.intro:
The Square Mile runs on air conditioning and coffee. We look after VRF systems in serviced offices, split systems in comms rooms, and the refrigeration behind the lunchtime trade — display cabinets, cold rooms and cellar cooling in pubs and restaurants.

Access and out-of-hours working are the norm here; we carry the permits, RAMS and insurance evidence building managers ask for.

fields.name: Westminster & West End
fields.intro: From Soho kitchens to Victoria offices, Westminster mixes heritage buildings with dense hospitality. Listed-building constraints on external plant are common; we design around them with low-profile condensers, acoustic enclosures and internal plant rooms.

fields.name: Southwark & Bermondsey
fields.intro: Borough Market traders, Bermondsey Street restaurants and the offices along the South Bank keep us busy in SE1. Display refrigeration and walk-in cold rooms dominate; we also maintain air conditioning for several converted-warehouse office buildings.

fields.name: Hackney & Shoreditch
fields.intro: Independent restaurants, bars and food producers in Shoreditch and Hackney need refrigeration that survives basement kitchens and tight sites. We fit compact cold rooms and cellar coolers and run pre-summer maintenance rounds across the borough.

fields.name: Stratford & Newham
fields.intro: Retail at Westfield and the surrounding food outlets, plus the new residential and office blocks around the Olympic Park. Display refrigeration maintenance and split-system installs are our most common jobs in E15 and E20.

fields.name: Islington & Camden
fields.intro: Upper Street, Camden Market and the King's Cross development bring a dense mix of restaurants, bars and offices. Cellar cooling repairs peak here every summer; we schedule pre-season services from April.

fields.name: Croydon
fields.intro: South London's largest commercial centre, with supermarkets, offices and a growing restaurant quarter around Boxpark. We maintain display refrigeration and air conditioning across the town centre and Purley Way retail parks.

fields.name: Ealing & Acton
fields.intro: West London food retail and hospitality, plus light-industrial units in Park Royal with process cooling and cold storage needs. Freezer room builds and pack-system maintenance are regular work here.

fields.name: Heathrow & Hounslow
fields.intro: Hotels and airport-adjacent logistics dominate around Heathrow. VRF maintenance across hotel bedrooms and temperature-controlled storage for freight forwarders are our core services in the area.

fields.name: Reading
fields.intro: Reading's business parks, data centres and town-centre hospitality extend our Berkshire coverage. We run PPM contracts for office VRF systems and close-control cooling for comms rooms along the M4 corridor.

fields.name: Slough & Windsor
fields.intro: Slough Trading Estate's food manufacturers and distribution units need cold storage that meets audit standards; Windsor's hotels and restaurants need discreet plant and quiet condensers. We cover both from the M4.

fields.quote: Cellar cooler died on a Friday in July. Rang at 6pm, engineer on site by half seven, kegs back to temperature before the evening rush. Fitted a new unit the following week at the price quoted.
We moved our VRF maintenance to Mehr Cool this year. The F-Gas paperwork is finally in order, the reports are clear enough to forward to tenants, and they turn up when they say they will.
Multideck kept icing up and two previous companies couldn't fix it. Mehr Cool found a failed defrost sensor in twenty minutes. Straightforward people who know their kit.
New walk-in built over two days between services with zero disruption. Temperature logger left running overnight and the report emailed the next morning. Exactly what we needed.
Duty/standby cooling for our comms room with automatic changeover. Clear explanation, tidy install, and the monitoring alerts have already caught one fault before it mattered.
Vaccine fridges and cold room serviced on schedule with the temperature records our inspector asked for. Responsive on the phone and honest about what does and doesn't need doing.
